about: Manual (by-hand / by-ear) test checklist for the SEQ V4+ fork and the MatriX. Shown in the seqemu web UI (Checklist window); results are saved per target (emu / hw) to manual-results.json next to this file. targets: which of emu / hw an item applies to.

items.title: Flash the SEQ firmware
steps: Build apps/sequencers/midibox_seq_v4 (bash, source_me_MBHP_CORE_STM32F4, make).
Upload project.hex with MIOS Studio.
Reboot.
items.expect: Boots, loads the session, no fault screen.

items.title: Flash OUR MatriX firmware
steps: Build apps/controllers/matrix (make).
Upload with MIOS Studio over the MatriX USB.
Keep the SD card in (it holds setup.txt).
items.expect: Boots to its logo, then the main page; no garbage menu item; no fault.

items.title: Start the emulator pair
steps: apps/sequencers/midibox_seq_v4/emu/run-with-matrix.sh
items.expect: SEQ panel + the real MatriX panel embedded; both show 'connected'.

items.title: MatriX finds the SEQ
steps: HW: cable SEQ O4/BLM <-> MatriX BLM1; SEQ Menu > MIDI > Misc: BLM port IN4 (save the session).
Emu: automatic (DIN 4 cable).
items.expect: MatriX OLED reads '1: Legacy BLM' with SEQ context lines below; Test Mode shows 'BLM 1 CONN' in green.

items.title: Calibrate the MatriX
steps: ≡ menu > Calibration > ✓.
Move every fader and both stick axes end to end until all rows turn green.
✓ = Commit.
items.expect: The stick dot reaches all four edges (columns 1/16, rows 1/16); Commit saves (survives a reboot).

items.title: Screen saver wakes from every surface
steps: Start the saver (MIOS Terminal: screen_saver, or wait the delay); press an SEQ button. Repeat waking it with: an encoder, a MatriX grid key, a MatriX fader, a MatriX panel button (A/B/‹/✓).
items.expect: Every one of them brings the normal LCD back at once (the press also does its normal job).

items.title: MatriX menu navigation
steps: Open ≡; push the stick down once, release, repeat to Test Mode; hold it up to go back to Main.
Same in Setup (≡ > Setup).
Enter Brightness, Setup, Calibration, Demos, Test Mode; ‹ back out of each.
items.expect: Each push = exactly one item, the list glides to centre it; holding repeats and stops at the first/last item; Test Mode reachable; no garbage 7th item; no crash. QUESTION: repeat speed right?

items.title: MatriX brightness
steps: Open ≡, select Brightness (corner reads 'Adjust ←X→'), sweep the X fader end to end; close the menu; power-cycle (hw) / restart (emu).
items.expect: The whole grid dims and brightens with 'Current N%' (5..100%); the setting is kept after a restart.

items.title: Full HIL suite on the hardware
steps: Don't flash while it runs. cd tests; pytest -q (see reference-build-and-flash).
items.expect: All green (emulator baseline: 323 passed / 4 skipped). Note any red test names here.

items.title: Enter RACK and read it
steps: Hold SHIFT (bottom-left key), tap left-column key 10.
items.expect: Columns = tracks 1-16, rows = rack rows (Ptch ... LFO); each row its own colour; live = bright, bypassed = dim pastel, empty = off.

items.title: Tap a pad = focus
steps: Tap a pad.
items.expect: SEQ jumps to the PROC page with that track + row focused (GP encoders operate it).

items.title: Double-tap = row on/off
steps: Double-tap a set pad (within ~350 ms).
items.expect: Row toggles bypass, same as the SEQ B-row double-tap. QUESTION: too destructive on Ptch/Tens (they reset dials)?

items.title: Extra row / extra column
steps: Tap extra-row keys (bottom).
Tap extra-column keys (left).
items.expect: Extra row selects tracks (mute/solo when that mode is latched); extra column focuses rows on the visible track.

items.title: Faders ride the dials
steps: Focus a row (e.g. Echo).
Move faders 1-4, Y, X.
items.expect: Fader n = the dial over GP n (1-4 = GP1-4, Y = GP5, X = GP6), full travel = full range; SEQ LCD + MatriX OLED follow. QUESTION: jump vs soft pickup? Is Y/X -> GP5/6 right?

items.title: Stick walks the rack
steps: Push the stick up/down, left/right; hold it.
items.expect: Up = the row above, down = below; left/right = previous/next track; holding repeats, faster with more throw.

items.title: A / B / stick press in RACK
steps: Focus LFO, press A twice.
Press B on a set row.
Press the stick.
items.expect: A flips the plane (CONF 1/2 <-> DEST 2/2); B toggles the row on/off; stick press = home on the first row. QUESTION: right mapping?

items.title: GRID on a melodic track
steps: SHIFT + left-column key 15 = GRID.
Play a melodic track.
items.expect: Steps run left -> right, pitches bottom (low) -> top (high); the playhead is a column sweeping left -> right.

items.title: Note colours
steps: GRID on a melodic track with notes at several pitches.
items.expect: Each pitch row its note colour (C red, D yellow, E green, F# cyan, G# blue, A# violet ...); playhead white; follows scrolling + force-to-scale.

items.title: Stick scrolls the grid
steps: Left/right, then up/down; hold.
items.expect: Left/right pages 16-step views ('Step View 17-32'); up = pitch window up a semitone ('Grid Notes from ...'); holding repeats faster with throw. QUESTION: repeat feel? With FTS should Y move by scale degree?

items.title: A / B in GRID
steps: Press A, then B; keep pressing B until it wraps back to Gate.
items.expect: A = next parameter layer, B = next trigger layer; the SEQ flashes the layer's NAME ('Trigger Layer / E Skip') and the MatriX OLED's Par / Trg lines follow every press.

items.title: Stick press = home
steps: Scroll away, then press the stick.
items.expect: Back to step view 1 and the default pitch window ('Grid home').

items.title: ‹ = EXIT, ✓ = play/stop
steps: From PROC press ‹.
Press ✓ twice.
items.expect: ‹ leaves PROC (EXIT); ✓ starts then stops the sequencer (in any mode, unless a capture is armed).

items.title: TRACKS mode
steps: SHIFT + left-column key 14 = TRACKS; play.
items.expect: Each track row its own hue, the playhead white; stick pages step views.

items.title: Faders outside RACK
steps: In GRID move a fader.
items.expect: Stock behaviour: sends its CC (option 30 / BLM fader config).

items.title: OLED context lines
steps: Switch between GRID, RACK, KIT, CAPTURE; scroll; move faders.
items.expect: OLED shows the mode, track, step view, pitch window, transport; in RACK the dial + value each fader rides, live.

items.title: Grid refresh at 100 Hz (2026-10-24)
steps: Play a pattern. In GRID, FULL, PLAY and RACK: tap pads fast, hold chords, move a fader, scroll with the stick, watch the playhead.
items.expect: Feels the same as before: presses light at once, the playhead moves smoothly, nothing lags. (The grid image is now recomputed every 10 ms or right after a MatriX input instead of every mS; it cost up to 43 % of the CPU.) QUESTION: anything feel slower?

items.title: Fast hit entry
steps: Visible track = a drum track; GRID mode.
Tap empty cells; tap an existing hit.
items.expect: Empty cell: the hit lands on press; tapping a hit removes it on release.

items.title: Hold a hit + fader 1 = velocity
steps: Hold a hit, move fader 1, release.
items.expect: 'Hit Velocity n' on the SEQ, the OLED shows it; the hit is KEPT (not removed). Needs a Velocity lane on the kit.

items.title: Accents, playhead, drum colours
steps: Play the kit; add an accent on the SEQ.
items.expect: Each drum row its colour; accented hits brighter; a soft-white playhead sweeps the empty cells.

items.title: Extra column plays drums
steps: Tap left-column keys; arm REC and tap again while playing.
items.expect: Each plays that row's drum (like the B-row 909 pads); with REC armed it records. It no longer selects tracks in the kit grid.

items.title: Enter the canvas
steps: SHIFT + left-column key 9.
Play a track for a few bars.
items.expect: Rows = tracks; the source row lights the grabbable bars, right-aligned (now = right); OLED 'CAPTURE src GxTy / grab up to N bars'.

items.title: Arm, then grab
steps: Tap a cell in another track's row.
Tap it again (or ✓).
items.expect: First tap only previews the span ('ARMED k bars -> Tn'); the second grabs ('Captured k bars -> Tn'); the copy sounds like what played.

items.title: Cancel and undo
steps: Arm a grab, press ‹.
Grab one, then UNDO on the SEQ.
items.expect: ‹ disarms (nothing written); UNDO restores the destination track.

items.title: Source + phase
steps: Tap a left-column key; tap extra-row key 1 (bottom-left of the extra row).
items.expect: Left column picks the source (visible track); extra-row key 1 toggles GRID (loop-aligned) / HEARD (ends at the playhead).

sections.title: MatriX — PLAY (piano roll over isomorphic keyboard)

items.title: Enter PLAY
steps: Select a melodic track. Hold SHIFT, tap extra-column key 8.
items.expect: Top half = the track's steps as a piano roll, bottom half = a lit isomorphic keyboard (blue = in scale, warm white = tonic, dark = out of scale). OLED: PLAY, page + FOLLOW, roll range, shape (e.g. '4ths J1 R5'), 'Keys from C-3'.

items.title: Play the keyboard
steps: Play pads on the bottom half; move up a row; play a pitch that appears twice.
items.expect: Sounds on the track (same feel as the B-row keyboard); the row above is a 4th up; every pad of a held pitch lights orange. Releasing always ends the note, even after switching mode with the pad down.

items.title: Play it in, watch it land
steps: Arm REC, start the sequencer, play a line on the bottom half.
items.expect: Notes appear in the roll on the top half as they record (if the window covers their range — stick Y moves it).

items.title: Edit on the roll
steps: Tap empty roll cells; tap one again; toggle the track's Force-to-Scale (Track Mode page).
items.expect: A tap adds that note at that step, a second tap removes it. FTS on = in-key rows (8 scale notes), off = chromatic rows with out-of-scale rows dimmed. Gld ties show as a pastel continuation.

items.title: Notes stay where you can see them
steps: On the roll: tap a note, then tap another pitch on the same step.
SHIFT + tap a third pitch on it; look at the EDIT page (panel) for that step.
Tap the chord's bottom note to remove it; record a fast run with REC armed and look at the EDIT page.
items.expect: A different pitch REPLACES the step's note (one note per step). SHIFT + tap adds a chord tone; the EDIT cell shows the note with a '+' and the panel stays on 'PA:Note' (no layer jump). Removing keeps a note on layer A. The OLED lists the step's notes. Any recorded chord tones show as '+' on EDIT.

items.title: Hold a step, play it in (picker)
steps: Hold a roll cell; play one key, then two more while still holding; release.
Hold two cells in different columns and play a key.
items.expect: The held cell turns white and its notes light on the keyboard. The first key replaces the step's note, later keys add a chord; keys sound but don't record at the playhead. Every held step gets the notes. Releasing does NOT toggle the cell.

items.title: Note length by span
steps: Hold a note's cell, tap a later cell on the same row; play it.
Hold the onset again, tap a cell to its LEFT.
items.expect: The note lasts until the tapped step (pastel continuation on the roll, held through on playback, stops before the next note). Tapping left = back to one step, the old continuation cleared.

items.title: Hold + faders
steps: Hold a note's cell, move fader 1, then fader 2; release.
items.expect: Fader 1 = the step's velocity, fader 2 = its length (LCD message shows the value); the note survives the release.

items.title: x2 / x2 empty / /2 on A and B
steps: In PLAY on a short loop: press MatriX A; then B; then SHIFT + B. Undo with SELECT + CLEAR on the panel.
items.expect: A: the loop doubles and the new half repeats it. B: doubles with the new half EMPTY (no old notes reappear). SHIFT+B: halves. LCD 'Length' message each time; stops at the track's maximum ('track max'); each step undoes.

items.title: Hold a page, tap another = loop
steps: On a 64+ step track: hold strip page 1, tap page 3; then hold page 2, tap page 4; run it.
items.expect: The strip lights the loop's pages green. A loop starting after page 1 plays the earlier pages once, then loops (MB's loop point). Growing leaves the new pages empty.

items.title: GRID rows follow the track's FTS
steps: Stock GRID (SHIFT + key 15) on a melodic track with Force-to-Scale OFF: tap up a column.
Turn FTS on and tap again.
items.expect: FTS off = every semitone reachable (chromatic rows); FTS on = scale rows. The OPT item 'BLM ... always use Force-To-Scale' is gone.

items.title: GRID taps on a transposed track
steps: GRID on a melodic track with a few notes; transpose it (Trn. page Semi +2, or hold a key with Transposed loops).
Tap a lit note to turn it off; tap an empty step; tap a lit step on another row; do the same in PLAY's roll.
items.expect: The grid shows the notes where they sound; tapping a lit note turns THAT note off (it used to jump up by the transpose); a new note lights exactly where you tapped.

items.title: Pages + follow
steps: Use a track longer than 16 steps, run it. Tap an extra-row page; push the stick left/right; press the stick.
items.expect: Extra row: green = in the loop, yellow = on view, red = playing elsewhere. Tap/stick X lock the view (OLED LOCK); stick press = FOLLOW again + roll home. Leaving PLAY puts the panel's own FOLLOW setting back.

items.title: Shape the keyboard
steps: SHIFT + stick X; SHIFT + stick Y. On the panel in INS view: GP1 = Jump, GP2 = row interval.
Try Jump 7 + rows 4 (Tonnetz) and FOLD + rows Oct (degree lines).
items.expect: SHIFT+X steps the row interval (LCD 'Grid keyboard rows' + the shape name), SHIFT+Y moves the keyboard an octave; the B-row keyboard moves with it (one shape).

items.title: Drum track in PLAY
steps: Focus a drum track while in PLAY. Tap hits on the top half; play the bottom rows left to right; hold a hit and tap a velocity pad on its row; push the stick up/down (16-drum kit).
items.expect: Top = kit (drum x steps), bottom = the SAME drums x 16 velocities (soft left, loud right), each drum's colour on both its rows. A velocity pad plays that drum at that velocity (records when armed) and its row shows the velocity as a bar. Hold a hit + velocity pad sets the hit's velocity and keeps it. Stick Y scrolls the 8-drum window; stick press = back to drum 1.

items.title: Enter FULL
steps: Melodic track: hold SHIFT, tap extra-column key 12; play up and down the grid.
items.expect: Rows 3-16 are the isomorphic keyboard (rows 9-16 identical to PLAY's keys); row 1 = scale/root picker, row 2 = chord strip. OLED: KEYS, shape, 'Keys from', velocity + root, the scale's name, the last chord + strip voicing.

items.title: Scale / root picker (row 1)
steps: Tap row-1 pads 1-12 (roots), 13 (Bus), 14/15 (scale -/+), 16 (A/B) while a force-to-scale track plays.
items.expect: The root pad lights gold and the scale's pitch classes teal; the keyboard's blue lights shift but every pad keeps its note; the playing FTS track follows the new key at once; Bus lights gold and hands the root to the transposer; 14/15 step the scale (LCD name); A/B flips between the last two scales. The choice survives a power cycle (config file).

items.title: Chord strip (row 2)
steps: Play row-2 pads 1-7 (triads) and 9-15 (7ths); tap pad 8 (inversion) and 16 (open/close) and play again; pick a pentatonic and look at the strip; arm REC and play a chord.
items.expect: Each pad plays its diatonic chord (roman numeral on the OLED); the chord's tones light orange on the keyboard so you can play over it; inversion/open revoice the next chords (the pads light while engaged); a pentatonic darkens degrees 6/7; with REC armed a chord lands on one step.

items.title: HOLD (toolbar 5)
steps: Toolbar 5 on; play a chord-strip chord and let go; play another; play a key; toolbar 5 off. Then HOLD on, latch a chord, switch to PLAY.
items.expect: Released chords keep sounding (still lit orange) until the next press replaces them; HOLD off or panic releases them; leaving FULL turns HOLD off and releases the latch.

items.title: Toolbar
steps: Extra row: keys 1/2 (octave), 3/4 (semitone), 6 (shape), 7 (FOLD), 8 (REC), 16 (panic) while holding a note.
items.expect: Octave/semitone move the keyboard (and light the direction you moved); shape cycles 4ths/5ths/Maj 3rds/Tonnetz (or Diatonic 4ths/Degree lines under FOLD) with an LCD name; FOLD toggles in-key; REC arms like the panel; panic silences everything and recentres bend/mod.

items.title: Stick + fader 1
steps: Hold a note, move the stick left/right and up; move fader 1, play again.
items.expect: Stick X bends the pitch and springs back to centre; stick up = mod wheel, back to 0. Fader 1 sets the velocity of the next notes (LCD 'Velocity: n').

items.title: Drum track in FULL
steps: Focus a drum track in FULL; play across a row, then down a column.
items.expect: Each row is a drum, soft on the left to loud on the right; records when REC is armed.

items.title: OLED names fader / stick moves (no CC flash)
steps: In GRID move fader 2, then in FULL move the stick and fader 1, then in RACK tap a row and move fader 1. Watch the MatriX OLED (hardware: needs the 2026-10-18 MatriX firmware).
items.expect: No full-screen 'CC n' flash. The OLED's bottom line says what the move did for about 1.5 s: 'F2 CC16 ch1 93' in GRID, 'JX bend +64' / 'JY mod 64' / 'F1 key vel 100' in FULL; in RACK the moved fader's own dial line gets a '>' ('1>Semi').

items.title: Hold a step = focus (PLAY roll + KIT hit)
steps: Panel on the EDIT page. In PLAY hold a roll cell that has a note: turn a GP encoder, move faders 1-3, release. Repeat in KIT with a hit.
items.expect: While held the LCD shows the LAYERS view of that step and comes back on release; faders ride Vel / Len / Roll (kit: Len then Note), the OLED lists them with a '>' on the moved one; the note / hit is still there after the release.

items.title: Kit accents over the hits
steps: KIT on a drum track with an Accent trigger layer: lay some hits, press B (Accent), tap a hit, tap it again, tap an empty cell, press B back.
items.expect: The hits never disappear when B switches layers. On Accent a tap turns the hit white (accent) / back; an empty cell gets hit + accent; on the gate layer the accents still show white.

items.title: HELP on the MatriX
steps: Hold SHIFT, tap bottom-row key 16. Tap zones, press A / B / stick, move a fader, hold SHIFT + tap left column 8 (PLAY), then press back.
items.expect: The grid shows coloured zones (picked one blinks white), nothing edits or plays; the OLED explains each control you touch; the map follows the mode; back leaves HELP. QUESTION: is the text readable / useful on the real OLED?

items.title: Kit editor finds the SEQ
steps: emu: header link Editor ↗ (or http://127.0.0.1:8080/editor). hw: flash first, then open apps/sequencers/midibox_seq_v4/tools/seq_editor.html in Chrome and allow MIDI.
items.expect: The header says Connected · <port> and shows the session; the left column lists the 16 tracks with the drum tracks lit and their first names; the emulator copy only picks an 'emu' port even with the real SEQ plugged in.

items.title: Rename a kit fast
steps: Pick a drum track. Type a name in drum A, Enter, keep typing down the column. Then Paste names… with a short list.
Look at the drum's name on the SEQ (TRKINST / Kit mode).
items.expect: Enter walks down the names; the SEQ shows each name at once; the yellow Unsaved pill appears; paste renames only the lines you gave.

items.title: Notes, velocities, audition
steps: Hold ▶ on a drum (and Shift+▶). With Audition edits on, spin a drum's note and drag its velocity.
On a kit with a Velocity layer / without an Accent layer, read the hints.
items.expect: The drum sounds while held and stops on release (also after changing its note mid-hold); edits play the drum; the dimmed columns match the hints. QUESTION: is audition-on-edit welcome or noisy?

items.title: Edits survive
steps: Rename a drum in the page, switch the group's pattern away and back. Repeat, but press Save to pattern and power-cycle instead.
Rename a drum on the PANEL keypad only, switch away and back.
items.expect: The names come back every time (the panel rename too — it used to be lost).

items.title: Kit library
steps: Save as kit (try an existing name). Library tab: open it, rename two drums, Save changes, Load into another drum track. Rename the file, then Delete it.
Check the target track's steps after the load.
items.expect: Overwrite asks first; the edited names load into the track; its steps are unchanged; rename refuses an existing name; the file is gone after Delete. Note/Chord presets show as not-a-kit.

items.title: Track tab
steps: Track tab, pick a melodic track: change channel, length, step length (tick Triplets), direction, Program. Switch play mode to Arpeggiator. Then pick a drum track.
Look at the same values on the SEQ's TRK pages.
items.expect: Each change shows on the SEQ at once (Program sends a program change); triplets reads 1/16T; Arpeggiator brings up the bus + transposer options; the drum track shows its Drum layers read-only; Type is read-only. QUESTION: anything you want editable that isn't?

items.title: Rack tab
steps: Rack tab: pick Echo on a track, turn Rpt and Vel; Bypass, Turn back on. Pick LFO, switch to DEST, tick Note. Pick PGen on a melodic track: Engage, then Roll.
Compare with the SEQ's PROC page for the same row and track.
items.expect: The grid cell goes green / amber with the row; the dial text matches the PROC page cell for cell (150%, Keyb, Q1/4); actions do what the encoder push does. QUESTION: is a grid of all tracks the right overview, or would you rather see one track's whole rack?

items.title: Names tab + copying
steps: Names tab: rename a pattern (category + name), a melodic track, and a captured phrase. Switch the pattern away and back; power-cycle for the phrase.
Track tab: Copy settings to another track. Kits tab: Copy kit to another drum track.
items.expect: The SEQ shows each name at once and keeps it; copied settings / kits match the source, the target's steps unchanged.

items.title: Mixer tab
steps: Mixer tab: with Live send on, change a channel's volume and pan for a synth that's connected.
Rename the map, Save to map (another slot), Load the first slot, Load the new one again.
Change something, then Load: the page warns about unsaved changes.
items.expect: The synth follows each change live; the saved slot comes back with its values and name; the SEQ's Mixer page shows the same values.

items.title: Song tab
steps: Song tab: build a short song (Play ×4 with patterns per group, a Tempo step, a Mutes step, Jump to position A1), name it, set a guide track above 4.
Save song, switch to another song and back; then play it in song mode.
Insert and delete a step.
items.expect: The SEQ's Song page shows the same steps; it plays as written; name and guide track (e.g. T7) come back after switching songs.

items.title: Rack faces (chord, zones, groove, generators)
steps: Rack › Pitch: set Bus to Sf, toggle notes of the hand-set chord with ChordMask strength up; listen.
Rack › Tension: click the zones.
Rack › Groove (Style = a Custom groove): edit delay / velocity steps, +I on a step, Save grooves.
Rack › PitchGen (engaged): lock steps and paint 0× / 2× multipliers while it plays.
items.expect: Each change is heard / seen on the SEQ's PROC page; locked steps stop changing; the groove comes back after a session reload.

items.title: Library: track presets of any type
steps: Library: Save a track (a melodic one) as a preset.
Load it into another melodic track with Settings ticked; then into a drum track (the page asks for Settings or Steps), then UNDO on the SEQ.
Load a kit into a drum track with only Name ticked.
items.expect: The target takes exactly the ticked parts; a different-type load turns the track into the preset's type; UNDO restores the track.

items.title: Info panel + Find a setting
steps: Hover around every tab: kit columns, Track settings, rack rows and dials, Names fields, Setup settings. Tab through with the keyboard too.
Press ? to hide and show the panel; narrow the window.
Track and Setup: type 'clock' into Find a setting, then Esc.
items.expect: Every control explains itself (what it does, where it is on the SEQ, ⚠ where it can interrupt playback); the panel sits at the bottom in a narrow window; Find leaves only matching settings and Esc brings everything back. Is the text right and readable?

items.title: Setup tab (global + session settings)
steps: Setup tab: change a few session settings (a tempo preset's BPM, Switch on, a T&A bus channel, clock in ports) and global ones (metronome channel, an Ui option). Watch the SEQ's own Options / BPM / MIDI pages.
Try LiveOctTranspose -2 and a groove selection with T9..T16 ticked.
Save to SD card for both files, power-cycle (or reload the session), Reload the tab.
items.expect: Each change shows on the SEQ's page at once; a tempo preset change on the current preset is heard right away; the ⚠ settings ask once; after the restart every value (including -2 octaves and T9..T16) is still there.

items.title: Setup: CV calibration test voltages
steps: With a CV interface configured, Setup › CV calibration: pick CV1, Test = 1 V, measure the output.
Test = Point 5; nudge its value with ±1 / ±16 and watch the meter; then Off.
Pick a mode again and leave the Setup tab; Save to SD card on the global file and restart.
items.expect: The output plays each test voltage and follows the nudges; Off and leaving the tab release it (the sequencer drives it again); the adjusted point is still there after the restart.

items.title: Setup: bookmarks + SysEx devices
steps: Setup › Bookmarks: rename bookmark 2 and 10, untick Mutes on one, change its page; Save both halves.
On the SEQ, tap those bookmark buttons; reload the session.
Setup › SysEx devices (needs /SYSEX/<DEV> folders): change a device's port and delay, then open the SysEx page on the SEQ.
items.expect: Taps jump to the edited page and leave the mutes alone where Mutes is unticked; names and settings survive the reload; the SysEx page shows the new port and delay.

items.title: Write: a chord progression onto a track
steps: Write tab: Am9 Dm9 G13 Cmaj9, Hold, tie on, 4 voices with bass; write onto a track that plays a pad synth; press PLAY.
Switch to Stabs (x..x..x.x..x..x.) and write again; then try ii7 V7 Imaj7 vi7 in F.
On the SEQ: change one voice on the EDIT page, sweep the rack's Tension; then UNDO.
items.expect: Each chord sounds once and is held (no retrigger every step); common tones ring across changes with tie on; stabs play the pattern; the voices move smoothly; the EDIT change and Tension act on it like any track; UNDO brings the old track back.

items.title: Write: SEQ chords + a root track
steps: Write tab, Write as SEQ chords + a root track: Cmaj7 Am7 Dm9 G13; chord track = one playing a pad synth, root track = a spare track, Bus 2; Write, PLAY.
Sweep the rack's Voicing dials (Sprd, Inv, Drop, Strm, Tilt) on the chord track, then the Tension row; play a key into Bus 2 from a keyboard.
UNDO on the SEQ.
items.expect: The chords sound like the voiced-notes version with the same smooth motion; every Voicing dial and Gravity act on it live; a keyboard key retransposes it; UNDO brings the chord track back.

items.title: Onboard keys play into a bus (#21)
steps: Set tab: Keyboard harmony, Set it up, PLAY.
On the SEQ select the Keys track; hold chords on the B-row keyboard, then on the MatriX PLAY / FULL keyboard.
Set it up again as Dark harmony; select the Keys track and hold single keys.
items.expect: Keyboard harmony: the pad plays what you hold, the bass its lowest note, the arp runs through it; letting go keeps the last chord. Dark harmony: the key you hold moves the harmony and its followers (C = as written). The Keys track itself never sounds.

items.title: Set: a starting point, then Restore
steps: Set tab: read the map and the warnings against what you know of the set.
Write > Progression: make chords. Set: Dark harmony, point the roles at spare tracks (pad/bass/arp on synths), Set it up, PLAY.
Hold keys on an external keyboard on the Keyboard channel (or select the Keys track and play the B-row); then Keyboard harmony; then Transposed loops (tick a few melodic tracks).
Restore. Reload the editor page (or open it in another browser) and check Restore is still offered while a backup exists.
items.expect: The map says in words what each track does; pad, bass and arp follow the harmony on the chord's own step; a held key moves harmony + melody + followers together; the modulator audibly sweeps; in Transposed loops the ticked tracks move with the key you hold, drums don't; Restore brings the tracks and the bus inputs back exactly (from the card if the browser lost its record: tracks only).

items.title: Set: demo sets (load, play the song, sections, keys)
steps: Emulator: the panel's Demos button (or Editor › Set › Demo sets). Browser version (lucasowens.github.io/mios32): its Demos button. Hardware: the editor on the SEQ's USB port, and the MBSEQ Demo Sounds set open in Live (tools/liveset; Live's MIDI prefs: SEQ Port 2 Track + Remote on).
Load Warehouse techno; when it says loaded, PLAY (Intro), then the section buttons (Drop, Break …).
Play the song and let it run through a few sections; Stop.
Select T11 (Keys) and hold a B-row / MatriX key while it plays.
Load the other three; load one twice (OK = open it as it is).
items.expect: Each demo makes its own session (DEMO_WH …) and leaves yours alone; sections switch all four groups; the song plays Intro → Outro at the demo's tempo and stops at the end; a held key moves the whole set; on the emulator every part sounds in the Sound window, and on the hardware in Live, each on its style's tracks (kit, bass, stab + echo, arp, pad, acid line with its filter sweeping, lead). By ear: do they sound like their style?

items.title: Live: the MBSEQ Demo Sounds set
steps: python3 tools/liveset/make_soundset.py, then open ~/Music/Ableton/Projects/MBSEQ Demo Sounds Project/MBSEQ Demo Sounds.als in Live 12.
Live › Settings › Link, Tempo & MIDI: MIDIbox SEQ V4+ (Port 2) input Track on, Remote on.
Load each demo from the editor (a fresh copy if it was loaded before 2026-10-25 21:00) and PLAY on the SEQ.
Acid: watch the Acid line track's filters in the Peak section.
items.expect: The set opens with no missing-file or error dialog; the drum rack shows 15 named 909 pads; each demo lights only its own style's tracks plus Drums 909, with no arming; the acid filters move with the CC74 LFO; nothing hangs or doubles. By ear: are the sounds right for each style (swap presets in make_soundset.py PARTS if not)?

items.title: Bus followers land on the chord change (#20)
steps: A root track: Note, port Bus 3, one note per bar (A, D, G, C), gate on the first step of each bar.
A melodic track: Transpose play mode on Bus 3 (MODE page), Hold on, a 16th line written around C-3, sounding on a synth.
A second melodic track: Pitch row ChordMask Str 127, Bus 3, fed by a harmony track with chords on Bus 3 instead. PLAY, listen at each change.
items.expect: The transposed line and the snapped line change on the first 16th of the bar, together with the root/chord - no one-16th smear of the previous chord on the downbeat (before the 2026-10-24 fix they were a step late).

items.title: Write: the progression generator
steps: Progression tool: pick a pad track and a melody track, switch Live on, PLAY.
Sweep Darkness, Strange, Colour, Motion; add Pedal and Lament; Reroll a few times; lock the chords you like and reroll again.
Try the variations: Use one, Morph → another, then turn the morph value on the SEQ (Morph page).
items.expect: Every knob turn is heard a moment later; locked chords never change; the modes get darker left to right; Strange leaves the key more; the morph glides the voices toward the variation; UNDO brings back the track as it was before Live.

items.title: Write: Bass & Arp
steps: Progression tool: a progression (e.g. Am9 Dm9 G13 Cmaj9). Bass & Arp: Offbeat bass onto a bass-synth track, up-down arp onto another; PLAY with the chords.
Try Acid with a few seeds and Slides 30 %; guide tones for the arp.
items.expect: Bass and arp follow every chord change; the same seed gives the same line; slides glide on a mono synth.

items.title: Write: Polyrhythm
steps: A drum track; Polyrhythm with the default lanes (4/16, 7/12, 3/7, 2/10) at 64 steps; Write; PLAY.
Change one lane's hits / rotate and write again.
items.expect: Each lane's drum plays its euclid cycle and drifts against the others; the kit's other drums keep their steps; UNDO takes the write back.

items.title: Write: MIDI clip
steps: In Live, drag a chord clip and a drum clip to the desktop.
MIDI clip: drop the chord clip onto a Note track and the drum clip onto a drum track; Write each; PLAY.
items.expect: The chords play as in Live (held notes held); the drum clip lands on the matching kit drums, unmatched notes are listed.

items.title: Write: Script
steps: Run each example (Acid line, Euclid kit, Chords from Roman numerals, Random walk melody) against suitable tracks.
Write a short script of your own; make a typo.
items.expect: Each write lands and plays; the log says what was written; a typo shows an error and writes nothing.

items.title: Editor: SEQ layout
steps: Header: switch to SEQ. Pick T1 (a drum track), press the GP keys under Evnt, Inst, Mode, Dir., Len., BPM, MIDI.
Menu: open Track Groove, CV Configuration, Bookmarks, Processor Rack, Tension Workbench; Exit (or Esc) back a few times.
Change a MENU shortcut on the Options page; switch back to Tabs.
items.expect: The LCD shows the same 5-letter shortcut names as the SEQ's MENU; each page shows only that page's settings for the lit track (a drum track adds its kit on Evnt / Inst); the changed shortcut shows on the LCD; Tabs comes back as it was.

items.title: Kits: from an Ableton rack
steps: Kits tab, a 16-drum track: From Ableton rack… → TR-909 LSO.adg (User Library › Presets › Instruments › Drum Rack); rename one drum, Apply with Also save as kit.
Play the track into Live's TR-909 LSO rack (MIDI track input = the SEQ port, the track's channel).
Try an 8-pad rack (DR-110 LSO) on the same track.
items.expect: Every drum triggers the matching pad in Live; the kit appears in the library as TR909LSO; the 8-pad rack changes only drums A–H and says so.

items.title: kitprint: TR-909 LSO onto the blackbox
steps: tools/kitprint: ./kitprint.sh print "TR-909 LSO"; do the four Live steps it prints; ./kitprint.sh slice …; ./kitprint.sh export blackbox … --to the blackbox SD card.
On the blackbox: load the preset, set Global In to the SEQ track's channel, play the TR-909 LSO kit from the SEQ.
Hit the closed and open hats in turn.
items.expect: slice reports 16 hits and no warnings; each pad sounds like Live's pad (same level balance, no clipped attack, no cut tail); note 36 is the bottom-left pad; the hats choke each other.

items.title: kitprint: a kit onto the S5000
steps: Format an image on the S5000 (SCSI emulator), take the card out.
./kitprint.sh export s5000 <kit> --image <the card's image>; card back in.
On the S5000: load the kit's folder, play it from the SEQ (notes 36-51), hit the closed then open hat.
items.expect: The program loads with 16 keygroups named TR909LSO …; every note plays its hit at the original pitch, whole (ONE SHOT) even with short gates; the hats cut each other (mute group).

items.title: kitprint: a kit onto the Salmple
steps: ./kitprint.sh export salmple <kit> --to <FAT32 stick>; plug the stick into the Salmple.
Load the new bank; trigger channels 1-8 (from the SEQ via the midiphy gates, or by hand).
items.expect: The bank shows the kit's tag + A/B; each channel plays the pad the export listed for it; no clipped attacks.

items.title: Panel buttons + LEDs
steps: Click round buttons and GP keys; ⌥-click (Option) to latch.
⌥-click Menu, then click a GP shortcut.
items.expect: Presses act like the hardware; LEDs follow the firmware; a latch holds until clicked again, or lets go by itself when the page changes (Menu + GP opens the page and Menu releases).

items.title: Encoders
steps: Scroll / drag GP encoders and the datawheel; click a knob.
items.expect: Turns step values; a click = encoder push.

items.title: LCDs + TPD
steps: Watch boot; play a track.
items.expect: Dot-matrix LCDs incl. bars/arrows; TPD scrolls the boot text, then VU meters while notes play.

items.title: Desktop windows
steps: Drag, resize, hide (✕), restore from the top bar, fit (⤢), Reset layout; refresh the page.
items.expect: Device windows keep their shape; the layout survives a refresh.

items.title: Joystick sensitivity
steps: MatriX window: set Stick far left; scroll the SEQ grid (GRID mode) with small drags; push through the MatriX menu; set it far right and repeat; refresh.
items.expect: Left = a long drag for full throw, small moves step one item at a time; right = twitchy short throw; the setting survives a refresh. QUESTION: which default feels right?

items.title: Snap to grid
steps: Turn Snap on; drag a window and resize another so their edges meet; refresh; turn Snap off and drag again.
items.expect: With Snap on a faint grid shows while moving and windows jump in 20 px steps, so edges line up exactly; the switch survives a refresh; off = smooth free movement.

items.title: Paint toggle
steps: Paint on; drag along GP keys and across the MatriX grid; start a stroke on a lit key.
items.expect: Each key passed gets one tap; starting on a lit key only erases; extra row/column never paint.

items.title: MIDI monitor + preview synth
steps: Play; tick 'preview synth'.
items.expect: Notes listed; the preview plays in time with no dropped or stuck notes.

items.title: Hear the SEQ in the web panel
steps: Open the panel, click anywhere once (browsers start audio only after a click), PLAY a set with drums, a bass, a pad and a melody — or Set tab: Dark harmony.
Watch the Sound window fill in: one row per track with the instrument it picked. Change one track's instrument and level; Volume, Reverb; Test.
STOP while a pad holds.
items.expect: You hear every track with zero setup — a kit for drum tracks (kick, snare, hats by drum name), bass, pad, pluck, lead or keys by track name / mode / register — even tracks that share a channel get their own sound; overlapping bass notes slide; STOP leaves nothing hanging.

items.title: Hear the CV outputs
steps: Set an unnamed melodic track's port to CV1 (channel 1) and a drum track's to CV1 channel 16 (the trigger outs); PLAY.
Watch the MIDI window and the Sound window.
items.expect: The MIDI window logs both as CV1; the melodic track sounds as the mono Eurorack-style voice (a resonant filter blip on each gate), the drum track as the kit. Naming the CV track Bass switches it to the bass.

items.title: Keyboard shortcuts
steps: Space, Esc, ← →, [ ], hold Shift over the MatriX.
Hold M, let go; then hold M and click a GP button (GP 7 = Trn.).
items.expect: Play/stop, exit, < / >, datawheel, MatriX SHIFT. Holding M shows Menu Shortcuts and lights the Menu key, letting go returns; hold M + GP jumps to that page, like Menu + GP on the hardware.

items.title: Hold-to-confirm actions (local + browser version)
steps: Event page (M + GP 2): hold GP 16 (INIT) with the mouse button down until it's done.
Hold Bookm. (⌥-click latches it) and hold a GP key for 2 s to store that bookmark.
Do both on the browser version too (lucasowens.github.io/mios32).
items.expect: The 'Hold for N seconds' countdown runs down and ends in 'Track has been initialized!' / 'Bookmark stored!'; the panel keeps running afterwards (the browser version used to freeze when the action fired).

items.title: Timing stats in the MIOS terminal
steps: Play a track routed to a DIN port (and MIDI clock out on a DIN port).
In MIOS Studio's terminal: timing reset, wait a few seconds, timing.
items.expect: DIN and RT counts grow with the music; the tick period is close to 60e6 / (BPM x 384) us truncated to whole us; nothing sounds different.

items.title: Multi-tempo baseline
steps: Save your session (the matrix refuses to leave unsaved changes).
Mute or unplug whatever listens on OUT3 or MIDI channel 16 (the USB flood goes there).
cd tests; python diag_timing.py --matrix (about 20 minutes).
items.expect: A table per scenario, tempo and class, and your session loaded back; record it in MBSEQV4_REFERENCE.md §1 (Output timing).

items.title: 96 kHz audio test
steps: MIDI-wire tap on DIN OUT1 (no receiver): 470 ohm between socket pins 4 and 5, pin 5 -> 10 kohm -> input 1 tip, tip -> 2.2 kohm (anything 470 ohm-2.2 kohm) -> ground (pin 2). Your cut cable: red = pin 5 (data), black = pin 4, shield = pin 2 (ground); white and green unused. DIN pins run 1-4-2-5-3 around the arc, pin 2 in the middle. Gate 1 (D1) or trigger 1 (D3) through a 10:1 divider into input 2.
Arm a 96 kHz stereo recording, then: cd tests; python diag_timing.py --rig --bpm 120 --secs 70. Export the take as WAV.
python audio_timing.py take.wav --bpm 120 --names midi gate. Repeat at 125 and 130 BPM.
Optional: one take with the drum module on OUT1 instead of the tap, to hear its own jitter added.
items.expect: The MIDI off-grid spread matches the on-chip DIN note-on spread for the same window (125 BPM tight, 120 and 130 about 1.4 ms); the gate spread matches DIG (about 1 ms). The logic analyzer waits until before #11.

items.title: DIN burst wire check (#6)
steps: Move the MIDI-wire tap to DIN OUT3 (whatever normally sits on OUT3 comes off) and arm a 96 kHz recording on input 1.
cd tests; python diag_uart_defer.py run (about 25 s; the transport starts and stops; OUT3's running-status setting is put back).
Stop the recording, export it as WAV, then: python diag_uart_defer.py check take.wav
items.expect: PASS: 0 framing errors; each burst complete and in order with 1 status byte (running status on) or 160 (off); a note-off for every note that started before the stops; strict on/off alternation through the sustained phase.

items.title: Exact tempo (#7)
steps: Optional long check: cd tests; python diag_timing.py --period (plays your session at 120, 128 and 133 BPM for an hour each; prints set vs measured period every minute).
Wire check: tap on OUT1, 96 kHz recording, python diag_timing.py --rig --bpm 130 --secs 70, then python audio_timing.py take.wav --bpm 130 --names midi.
Turn the BPM wheel back and forth while a track plays.
items.expect: --period stays within a few ppm (the timebase's own clock); the take's 16th sits ~62 ppm under the exact nominal (the interface clock), not on the old whole-us figure; the wheel never makes the beat jump ahead.

items.title: Run-ahead feel (#8)
steps: Use a tight receiver (not the blackbox: it adds ~1 ms RMS of its own; measure a module with diag_timing.py --rig --note N --mirror 3 first).
Play a groove; turn knobs, mute / unmute and transpose live while it plays.
A/B in the MIOS terminal: timing ahead 0 (stock), timing ahead 3000 (default).
items.expect: Live controls still feel immediate (they land 3-5 ms later); the groove is at least as tight with run-ahead on.

items.title: IIC items after the rest of a tick (#27)
steps: In your own session (clock to all ports, IIC MIDI ports in use), put 16ths on DIN OUT1.
cd tests; python diag_timing.py --bpm 130 --secs 30 (your session as it is).
items.expect: DIN note-ons ~50 us late (was ~350 us with IIC clocked); the IIC gear still plays and stays in time.

items.title: Clock ahead of a busy DIN port (#9, 2026-10-25)
steps: Clock a drum machine from a DIN port that also carries dense notes / CCs (e.g. an LFO CC track to the same port).
Listen for swing / wobble against the SEQ; optionally the MIDI tap on that port: python audio_timing.py --decode.
From tests/: python -m pytest apps/seq_v4/test_uart_rt_lane.py
items.expect: The clocked machine stays tight however busy the port is; 0xF8 on the wire within ~0.64 ms of its tick; the pytest passes.

items.title: Stop never adds a hit or a clock step (#12 slice, 2026-10-25)
steps: Clock an external sequencer or clock divider from a SEQ clock output (and/or play drums from D3 triggers / CV gates).
Start and stop the SEQ 20-30 times at random moments, a few times with STOP double-tapped and once with UNDO while playing.
From tests/: python -m pytest apps/seq_v4/test_stage_cancel.py
After any session of mashing the panel while playing: python -c "from harness import Board; print(Board().midiout_watch())" (who made the MIDI task wait longest).
items.expect: The external sequencer stays in step with the SEQ after every stop (no extra step); no drum hit right after STOP; the pytest passes.

items.title: Pulse widths + panel first (#13, 2026-10-25)
steps: Play the TIMING rig (or CV gates / clock outputs / triggers) at 120 and 133 BPM. Hold buttons, tap fast, switch pages, mute tracks; watch the GP LEDs.
Afterwards, from tests/: python -c "from harness import Board; b = Board(); print(b.srio_stall())"
items.expect: No GP LED flicker; holds and taps normal. srio_stall: stalls 0, refused 0. Clock and trigger pulses last their set width (pulse_stats mean ~60 us late).

items.title: Gates AT the tick (#13 full, 2026-10-25)
steps: Play CV gates / clock outputs (the TIMING rig) at 120 and 133 BPM. Hold buttons (held steps, UTILITY + GP, instrument instantiation), tap fast on EDIT / MUTE, watch the LEDs, play the MatriX.
items.expect: Panel unchanged: holds never drop, no missed or doubled presses, no flicker. On-chip DIG mean ~0 us (latched at the tick); CV ~0.36 ms ahead of its gate. If holds misbehave: board.cv_stage(False) to A/B.

items.title: Gates on the tick (#13 stage 1, 2026-10-24)
steps: Play the TIMING rig (or any CV/gate set) at 120 and 133 BPM. Mash buttons on EDIT / MUTE, turn encoders, watch the LEDs and the MatriX.
Optional bench: a gate output through a divider into Scarlett input 2, the MIDI tap on input 1; python diag_timing.py --rig --bpm 130 --secs 70, then audio_timing.py.
items.expect: Panel unchanged (no missed or doubled presses, no encoder jumps, no flicker). On-chip DIG ~0.2 ms after the tick (was 1.2-2.4 ms); on the audio test the gate lands a steady ~0.2 ms after its MIDI note-on.

items.title: USB transfer on queue (#19, refined 2026-10-25)
steps: cd tests; python diag_usb_timing.py --bpm 130 --secs 30 (plays the TIMING rig on USB1: pass, package, stock).
python diag_usb_timing.py --bpm 130 --secs 20 --chords
items.expect: pass and package: much smaller off-grid spread than stock (the 1 ms re-grid gone). Chords: pass delivers every chord in one transfer (spread 0) with the first notes on time; package splits them ~0.4 ms.

items.title: Slicer act 2
steps: Chok, Motn (5-detent), 1stp grid, CHOP jump pads, ORDR paint plane, punch-chop, momentary interject, read-head wink (plan 2026-07-17-slicer-act2).
items.expect: Each sounds/feels right; note any that don't.

items.title: Capture-fidelity feel pass
steps: Freeze echo / LFO / swung / direction tracks while STOPPED; copy them.
items.expect: The copy sounds identical (those dials now travel).

items.title: Drum tape pitch + transpose
steps: Capture a kit with a Note lane while playing; transpose a drum track and copy it.
items.expect: Heard pitch captured; transpose travels with the copy.

items.title: 2026-10-02 review fixes
steps: Phrase morph Loop A past 127; INS keyboard transpose sign; EDIT GP5 Kit view on a melodic track (should do nothing); slicer pass-through while holding.
items.expect: No clamp artefacts; sign shown correctly; Kit view only on drum tracks; held slicer keeps playing.

items.title: Robotize ranges inert at 0
steps: Fresh track, FX Robotize: turn the range dials without raising probability.
items.expect: Nothing happens until probability > 0 (07-18 change). QUESTION: is that what you want?
